title: Finite Gibbs spectral-tail energy Markov audit
question: Can the local Gibbs spectral complement be bounded by positive shifted-energy moments at every finite cutoff, providing the missing quantitative input for the cutoff-aware two-stage shell route?
method: Build the same zero-source oscillator Gibbs states as R-393 on dimensions 3 through 10 at volume 3 and higher feasible controls at volumes 4 and 5.
For each one- and two-site core, shift the local Hamiltonian by its computed spectral minimum and form the positive operator K and spectral projector P_E for every declared positive energy window.
Compute the complement mass Tr(rho Q_E), the K-weighted tail Tr(rho K Q_E), and the first and second moments from explicit reduced Gibbs matrices.
Check the finite inequalities tail <= Tr(rho K)/E and weighted_tail <= Tr(rho K^2)/E, retain per-cutoff profiles, projector errors and all orientation/core/beta rows.
Rebuild spectra, traces and profiles in a non-importing independent lane, apply a zero-moment hostile mutation, and compile the scalar Markov identities in Lean R394.
finding: The primary lane passes 13281/13281 checks and the non-importing independent lane passes 6/6. The integrated verifier passes 22/22 with Lean R394 compiling over 13 systems, 158 core layouts, 3160 spectral-tail rows and 240 cutoff profiles. Every shifted local energy is positive within tolerance; projector splits and both Markov inequalities have zero violations. The mass-tail range is -3.150593512508445e-16 to 0.857090394095672 and the weighted-tail range is -4.896283282882488e-16 to 4.223723806110137. Maximum first and second moments are 4.247282023186985 and 29.47317200298245. Adjacent cutoff ratios reach 16.93594199558396 for mass and 10.577916988017394 for the weighted tail. A hostile zero-moment mutation at V=5,d=4,beta=2 leaves a selected tail of 0.19203834045679757 against a zero bound and is caught.
decision_reason: R-394 advances the cutoff-aware route by isolating an exact finite Markov inequality and exposing its true missing premise: a cutoff-independent bound on local energy moments. Fixed windows can contain the full low-dimensional spectrum and then acquire high-energy states as the cutoff grows, so the finite inequalities cannot be promoted. The next candidate is an analytic moment bound or a physically normalized cutoff-dependent window compatible with the common form core.

adversarial_review.check: The minimum eigenvalue is computed from each local Hamiltonian and the smallest shifted eigenvalue is checked nonnegative.
Each energy window is built from computed spectral vectors and projector idempotence and positive rank are checked.
Window and complement masses are both retained and their sum is checked without clipping.
The actual mass and weighted tails are compared with first and second moments divided by the positive threshold.
Dimensions three through ten at volume three and higher feasible volume-four/five controls are executed.
Low-dimensional zero tails are retained as finite data and are not interpreted as uniform convergence.
Per-dimension maxima and adjacent ratios are retained so cutoff growth is not hidden by averaging.
The independent lane rebuilds the spectra, reductions, moments and profiles without importing the primary module.
Replacing the first moment by zero produces a visible false bound and is caught.
Lean checks scalar Markov inequalities only; spectral calculus, traces and limits remain Python/open analysis.
Moment/cutoff uniformity, Gibbs complement, shell summability, common core, beta/eta independence, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Prove a cutoff-independent local first/second or exponential energy-moment bound, or explicitly normalize a cutoff-dependent window, then combine it with the high-cutoff QCMI plateau. If neither route survives, record the obstruction without promoting common alpha.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Gibbs spectral-tail energy audit only. It proves no cutoff-independent moment bound, shell modulus, Gibbs complement theorem, cutoff/source/volume/shape bound, common core, beta/eta-independent topology, domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: A finite positive-energy Markov inequality is an exact finite bound; its usefulness for the main proof requires a separate uniform moment estimate.
